title: Repo/service metadata (C07 + headline-technology) — DESCRIBES owner-map.json
description: Per-repo ownership and display metadata. CONSUMED by monitor/lifecycle.mjs: `team` -> record.bugBelongsTo, `technology` -> record.repoTechnology (else humanize(repo)), `visibleTo` else $defaults.visibleTo -> record.bugVisibleTo. Note the verb in the title: this schema DESCRIBES the file, it does not validate it — no code loads this document, and the only references to its path are its own $id and owner-map.json's former claim to be validated by it. owner-map.json's $notConsumed block records that alongside the other capabilities this pair advertised and did not have.

$scope.description: Which area this map applies to. lifecycle.mjs joins on the BARE repo directory name, so an unscoped map attributes a team and a technology headline to any like-named repo in ANY registered area (docs, web, api-gateway). rollup.mjs passes the area being rolled up; on a mismatch the map is not applied at all, because a null bugBelongsTo is a state the contract already allows and a wrong one is not.

area.description: registry area slug these repos belong to

$defaults.description: Applied when an entry omits the field. Genuinely read by lifecycle.mjs — changing a value here changes behaviour.

$notConsumed.description: Standing record of fields and capabilities this file once documented and did not have. Kept in the artifact rather than only in a commit message, because the claims were read as true for over a month.

technology.description: Headline name/technology (e.g. 'Keycloak 26.7 (Quarkus)'). Written to record.repoTechnology; falls back to humanize(repo) if absent. NOTE: nothing renders repoTechnology today — see $notConsumed.rendering.

role.description: optional architectural role (edge/infra/...). Stored, read by no consumer — see $notConsumed.role.

visibleTo.description: default bugVisibleTo for findings in this repo

infra.description: Infrastructure components, deliberately OUTSIDE repos{}. The consumer looks up by scanned repo directory name and no scan produces `_infra_postgres`, so holding these in repos{} made structurally unreachable rows look like live mappings. No reader yet; a real join key (image name, against image-acceptance.json images{}) is what would give them one.

x-consumers: monitor/lifecycle.mjs assembleLifecycle() is the ONLY reader, via ctx.ownerMap from monitor/rollup.mjs; its output lands in lifecycle.json. Measured 2026-08-03: no renderer reads repoTechnology, bugBelongsTo or bugVisibleTo out of that artifact — admin/index.html reads lifecycle.json for SLA breaches and lifecycle state only. This key replaces an x-front-end-wiring note that described a C11 'lifecycle-tab.mjs' (no such file exists) plus C14 md / C31 pdf renderers that emit none of these fields.
